body.statement: Uniformly over \(c\in\mathcal C\), \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\|\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau(c)-\tau(c)\}-n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n(\psi^\theta_c(O_i),\psi^W_c(O_i),\psi^K_c(O_i))\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Jointly, the two implemented-rule evaluation errors satisfy \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}|\sqrt n\{\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-W(\widehat\theta_c)\}-n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi^W_c(O_i)|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and the analogous statement with \(K\) and \(\phi^K_c\). Therefore the full stack converges in \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\) to \(G\) with kernel \(\Gamma\), and at every finite deterministic collection of penalty coordinates the optimizer coordinates jointly attain the semiparametric covariance bound generated by \(\psi_c^\theta\). On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax submodel, set FangRidderXie2026's optimization penalty to \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), so its reported preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). This is the uniform-in-penalty extension of the fixed-penalty efficient influence bound in its Theorem 1 and the efficient doubly robust optimizer limit in its Theorem 5.
body.justification: On the common softmax submodel, a decision maker sees and selects from the whole preference curve; the contribution is the joint uniform process under explicitly maintained path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature, built on quantitative foldwise same-sample-path replacement.
body.gap: FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 1 gives the efficient influence function and bound, while Theorem 5 gives the efficient doubly robust optimizer and its limit at fixed optimization penalty \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}>0\). Restricting its admissible-rule framework to \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\) and mapping \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), equivalently \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), the gap is a joint uniform oracle-and-implemented frontier process under separately stated stronger path-uniform regularity; generic indexed Z-estimation supplies tools but not this verified composition.
body.consumer: The commitment-savings frontier in FangRidderXie2026 can be reported on the common regular softmax submodel with correlated uncertainty for every displayed preference rather than unrelated pointwise standard errors.
body.proof_tex:
We first connect the causal and observed-law objects.  Consistency and conditional exchangeability imply
\(m_a(X)=E[Y(a)\mid X]\).  Therefore, for every fixed \(\theta\),
\[
 E_P[v_\theta(O)\mid X]
 =\sum_a\pi_\theta(a\mid X)m_a(X)
   +\sum_a e_a(X)\frac{\pi_\theta(a\mid X)}{e_a(X)}
      E[Y-m_a(X)\mid A=a,X]
 =\sum_a\pi_\theta(a\mid X)m_a(X),                            \tag{20}
\]
where division is justified by overlap.  Hence \(Pv_\theta=W(\theta)\).  The divergence summand has expectation \(K(\theta)\) by definition.  Differentiation is dominated by the bounded softmax derivatives, bounded outcomes, overlap, and compactness.  The population first-order condition therefore gives
\[
 PD_c=\nabla W(\theta_c)-c\nabla K(\theta_c)=0,                \tag{21}
\]
and the five blocks of \(\Psi_c\) are centered.

The resolved foldwise replacement theorem and the product-rate condition imply, uniformly in \(c\),
\[
 \sqrt n\,\nabla\widehat M_c(\theta_c)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nD_c(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1),               \tag{22}
\]
and the derivative laws in (14)--(16) hold.  Uniform localization and the boundary distance \(\rho\) put every empirical maximizer in the interior with probability tending to one.  Thus its empirical gradient is zero.  With \(u_c=\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c\), the vector line-integral identity is
\[
 0=\nabla\widehat M_c(\theta_c)
   +\left\{\int_0^1\nabla^2\widehat M_c(\theta_c+tu_c)\,dt\right\}u_c. \tag{23}
\]
Uniform Hessian consistency, localization, smoothness, and the curvature floor give
\[
 \sup_c\left\|\int_0^1\nabla^2\widehat M_c(\theta_c+tu_c)dt+H_c\right\|
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1),\qquad \sup_c\|H_c^{-1}\|\leq h^{-1}.     \tag{24}
\]
Equations (22)--(24) first give \(\sup_c\sqrt n\|u_c\|=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\), and then
\[
 \sup_c\left\|\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)
 -n^{-1/2}\sum_iH_c^{-1}D_c(O_i)\right\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1).    \tag{25}
\]
The sign is positive because the matrix in (23) converges to \(-H_c\).

For the value paths, the same replacement calculation at \(\theta_c\) gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat W(\theta_c)-W(\theta_c)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_i\phi_c^W(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1),\quad
 \sqrt n\{\widehat K(\theta_c)-K(\theta_c)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_i\phi_c^K(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1),               \tag{26}
\]
uniformly in \(c\).  Taylor's identity, (16), and (25) give
\[
 \widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-W(\theta_c)
 =\widehat W(\theta_c)-W(\theta_c)+a_c^\top u_c+o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}), \tag{27}
\]
uniformly; the analogous formula holds with \(K,g_c\).  Combining (25)--(27) yields exactly the three-coordinate expansion with influences
\((\psi_c^\theta,\psi_c^W,\psi_c^K)\).

To distinguish implemented-rule evaluation from oracle-path estimation, subtract the population Taylor formula
\(W(\widehat\theta_c)-W(\theta_c)=a_c^\top u_c+o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\)
from (27).  This cancels the optimizer term and proves
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-W(\widehat\theta_c)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_i\phi_c^W(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1).                \tag{28}
\]
The same subtraction proves the asserted divergence expansion.  This verifies that the causal oracle target, its observed-law estimator, and evaluation of the random implemented rule are distinct objects.

It remains to establish the process limit.  Differentiating the population first-order condition and using (24) gives
\(\theta_c'=-H_c^{-1}g_c\); bounded derivatives and compact \(\mathcal C\) therefore imply a deterministic envelope \(C\) such that
\[
 \sup_c\|\Psi_c(O)\|\leq C,qquad
 \|\Psi_c(O)-\Psi_t(O)\|\leq C|c-t|                           \tag{29}
\]
almost surely.  For any finite collection of coordinates, the characteristic function expansion
\(E\exp\{iu^\top Z/\sqrt n\}=1-(2n)^{-1}u^\top E[ZZ^\top]u+O(n^{-3/2})\), valid because \(Z\) is bounded and centered, proves convergence to the centered Gaussian vector with covariance inherited from \(\Gamma\).  Tightness follows by covering \(\mathcal C\) by dyadic grids and applying the same symmetrized maximal inequality as in (9) to the increments in (29); the tail of the grid telescoping series is uniformly negligible.  Hence
\[
 n^{-1/2}\sum_i\Psi_\cdot(O_i)\Rightarrow G
 \quad\text{in }C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}.                           \tag{30}
\]
Equations (25)--(28) and (30) prove the full stacked conclusion and the covariance formula.

At any fixed finite set of penalties, \(\psi_c^\theta=H_c^{-1}D_c\) is the fixed-penalty efficient influence stated in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}frx\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}efficiency}\) after restricting to the common finite-action softmax submodel and setting
\(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\).  Stacking pathwise derivatives shows that every linear combination over finitely many coordinates has influence equal to the same linear combination of these blocks; hence its variance is the joint semiparametric covariance bound.  Expansion (25) attains it.  Finally Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}frx\mbox{-}penalty\mbox{-}map}\) gives
\(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\).  The fixed-penalty doubly robust attainment used in the comparison is the cited conclusion
\(\mathrm{lem{:}frx\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}dr\mbox{-}attainment}\), establishing precisely the stated fixed-to-uniform comparison.
